title: consolidate-credential-pipelines-and-lightweight-stream-operators
author: Priya Sharma
release_notes: Adds credential preset pipelines and a lightweight stream operator layer across Py/TS/Go SDKs. Minor version bumps: py 1.9.0, ts 2.3.1, go 1.8.4. No API breaking changes; improves retry ergonomics and stream handoff stability.
body:
Summary: Consolidates three previously divergent auth helper implementations into a small set of credential pipelines (preset, delegator, and fallback) and introduces a lightweight StreamOperator abstraction that sits between SDK transport and user async iterables. Motivation: Multiple SDKs kept reimplementing the same credential chaining and streaming glue which made parity, testing, and telemetry difficult. This PR centralizes the auth flow patterns and standardizes the stream handoff surface so SDKs have a consistent developer experience while allowing transport-specific optimizations.

Changes (high-level):
- Introduce credential pipeline presets (Preset, Delegator, Fallback) with a common semantic contract across Py/TS/Go. Presets encapsulate TTL, prefetch, and backoff hints.
- Add StreamOperator (lightweight) that: normalizes chunk envelopes, handles graceful pause/resume hooks, exposes a small backpressure hint API, and integrates with credential lifecycle events for preemptive refresh.
- SDK updates: Python adapter (redwood-sdk-python) exposes CredentialPreset and StreamOperator classes; TypeScript adds equivalent types and generator helpers; Go adds thin interfaces and a small concrete shim for iterator adapters.
- Retry ergonomics: new default retry profile bundles for streaming (latency-aware) and auth-fallthrough profile.
- Telemetry: emit credential pipeline events (prefetch, swap, fallback) and stream operator metrics (paused_duration, resume_count) to existing SDK telemetry hooks.
- Tests: integration matrix that exercises preset combinations and stream operator pause/resume across transports (http/ websocket).

Commits (summary):
- 9 commits, squashed on merge. Key commits: initial crosslang design and interfaces; python implementation + tests; ts implementation + typings; go shim and examples; telemetry hooks; docs and examples; CI fixes.

Files (representative):
- sdk/python/redwood/auth/presets.py (new)
- sdk/python/redwood/stream/operator.py (new)
- sdk/python/tests/test_stream_operator_integration.py (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/auth/presets.ts (new)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream/operator.ts (new)
- sdk/go/credential/preset.go (new)
- sdk/go/stream/operator_shim.go (new)
- docs/sdk/streaming-operators.md (new)
- examples/multi-sdk/credential-pipeline-demo/* (added small demos)

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked and reviewed (ENG-9142)
- [x] Implementations in Python/TS/Go
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Telemetry hooks wired
- [x] Examples and docs updated
- [x] Version bumps and changelogs updated

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- The StreamOperator deliberately stays minimal (only pause/resume/backpressure hint and lifecycle callbacks) to avoid locking SDKs into an opinionated runtime. We avoided adding batching semantics here because batching is runtime-specific and should remain in the serving-layer.
- CredentialPresets are intentionally lightweight descriptors (TTL, prefetch boolean, fallback order) not executors; actual execution is in each SDK's credential adapter so customers can plug KMS/HSM logic.

Review thread (selected):
- Dylan Price (review): "Overall direction looks solid. Two asks: 1) clarify interactions between StreamOperator.pause() and transport-level read loops to avoid deadlock; 2) ensure telemetry tags include preset name for downstream aggregation."
- Priya (author): "Added clarifying comments and updated operator.pause() docstring to mention non-blocking semantics and expectation that callers call resume(). Telemetry tags now include preset_name and chain_id."
- Maya Chen (review): "TS typings look good. Suggest renaming 'delegator' to 'cascade' in TS to match internal naming."
- Priya: "Renamed TS symbol to CascadePreset; kept python/go name 'Delegator' to avoid larger refactors in other packages in this PR. Filed follow-up ENG-9201 to align names across repo."
- Arjun Rao (review): "Go shim needs an explicit noop implementation for old iterators to avoid nil pointer panics in older Go SDK users."
- Priya: "Added shim with fallback noop that logs debug event when old iterator is used; added test covering nil shim case."

CI and iteration: 
- Initial CI run: build failures in ts unit tests due to a timing-dependent generator test flake; python lint flagged a stray TODO in presets.py.
- Follow-up: tightened TS test to reduce timing assumptions (use deterministic test clock), removed TODO and addressed linter comments. Final CI: all checks pass (unit, integration, linters).

Backward compatibility: 
- Exposed types are additive; no existing public method signatures were removed. We bumped minor versions for each SDK (Python 1.9.0, TypeScript 2.3.1, Go 1.8.4) to reflect added features. Migration doc added at docs/sdk/upgrade-1.9.0.md.

Telemetry & observability: 
- Added new events: credential.pipeline.prefetch, credential.pipeline.swap, stream.operator.paused_duration_ms, stream.operator.resume_count. These plug into current SDK telemetry sinks and are opt-in via existing telemetry flags.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- ENG-9201: name normalization across SDKs (Delegator -> Cascade)
- ENG-9302: evaluate adding optional batching helper in StreamOperator for dedicated environments
- ENG-9344: expose higher-level retry composer for auth fallthrough scenarios

Merge outcome: Merged via squash after approvals from Dylan and Maya. Merge commit message summarized design, tests, and version bumps. CI green at merge time.

Notes for release engineer: bump SDK packages and publish new changelogs. Python wheel: update setup.cfg extras to include new telemetry events. TypeScript: publish v2.3.1 and update package readme examples. Go: tag v1.8.4 and run module tidy.

Contact: Priya Sharma (author) for follow-ups and to coordinate the naming sweep (ENG-9201).
